block1.title: Help us explore premenstrual disorders across the menstrual cycle
block1.subtitle: Premenstrual disorders, including Premenstrual Syndrome (PMS) and Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD), can have severe effects on daily life. Help us understand how wearable data such as sleep, activity, and heart rate relates to PMDD.

blocks.title: Overview
blocks.content:
PMS clinically affects around 1 in 3 people who menstruate, and PMDD clinically affects around 1 in 20 people who menstruate. These conditions are characterised by physical and emotional symptoms that heighten during the luteal phase (the time between ovulation and menstruation).

The Cycle Study aims to improve understanding of why premenstrual disorders occur and how to provide better support and treatment.

block1.title: Who Can Take Part?
block1.content:
To take part in the Cycle Study, you must own a wearable device and have been diagnosed with PMDD.

You must also:
- Be aged 18 or over
- Live in the UK
- Be fluent in English
- Not be on hormonal contraception
- Not be pregnant or breastfeeding

block2.title: About the Cycle Study
block2.content:
The Cycle Study, led by researchers at King's College London (KCL), explores how PMDD fluctuates across the menstrual cycle and how it is influenced by environment, co-occurring conditions, and broader indicators of health.

To do this, we combine questionnaire data with wearable device insights such as sleep and activity patterns.

blocks.title: What Happens After You Sign Up
blocks.content:
After filling out the sign-up form, you will be asked to:
- Complete a screening questionnaire to check eligibility
- Read the Information Sheet
- Provide consent
- Connect your wearable so we can securely collect activity, sleep, and health data
- Complete daily and weekly questionnaires for two menstrual cycles or a maximum of 10 weeks (whichever comes first) via the Active app

items.title: Am I eligible?
items.content: If you are aged 18 or over, live in the UK, are fluent in English, and have PMDD, you may be eligible. If you are currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or on hormonal contraception, you are not eligible.

items.title: How do I sign up?
items.content: Click the Join Study button and follow the steps to create an account, read the Information Sheet, give consent, and complete the initial questionnaire.

items.title: I own a wearable. What devices are eligible?
items.content: Examples include Apple Watch (with iPhone via HealthKit), Fitbit, Garmin, and Oura.

items.title: Which wearable data will you collect?
items.content: With your permission, we will collect passive data such as daily activity, sleep duration and quality, and heart-rate metrics from your connected wearable or health app.
